title: Growth docs
intro: Growth handles your website's tracking pixels, cookie consent, conversion events, your own analytics and site-wide SEO (robots.txt, verification tags, IndexNow and an SEO checklist), plus a notice bar. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. Those pages write into your website's real database, so visits you make there are counted. There is no test mode.
script: Add the page script to the head of every page, before the other products' scripts, so it hears their shop events. It shows the consent banner and the notice bar, loads your tags once the visitor consents to their category, and records anonymous analytics. Everything it does follows the features that are on; with none on, it does nothing.
consent: The consent banner asks for two categories besides the necessary one: analytics and marketing. The visitor's choice is kept in their own browser (localStorage, asked again after 12 months) and never sent to us. Google Consent Mode v2 starts with everything denied and is updated with the choice. Tags load only after consent to their category: Google Analytics and analytics scripts need analytics; the Meta and TikTok pixels, Google Ads and marketing scripts need marketing; the Tag Manager container loads after either, and Consent Mode tells its tags what was granted. Using your own consent tool instead? Leave the banner off and pass the choice on with SSGrowth.consent.set().
privacy: Analytics are anonymous: no IP address, user agent, cookie or cross-site id is ever stored. A page view keeps the path (never the query string), whether it starts a visit (the start time of the visit is kept in the visitor's sessionStorage, never an id), the referring site or campaign, a device class from the screen width and the country your host's request header gives (x-vercel-ip-country, cf-ipcountry or cloudfront-viewer-country; turn country off in Settings). With 'Count only after analytics consent' on (the default), nothing is recorded before the visitor consents to analytics. Your server may also send a visitor's events itself: POST /v1/collect with the server token and no Origin, naming the visitor's IP address in SS-Visitor-IP (used only for the per-visitor limit, never stored). The country then comes from the headers our host sets for your server's request, so it is your server's country, not the visitor's; turn country off if you send events this way.
storage: Everything recorded goes into your own database (Connections → Database): raw events in ss_growth_events, removed by the database's expiry index after the retention you set (13 months by default; a change applies to events recorded afterwards), and daily totals in ss_growth_daily, kept forever. Days are the days of your business time zone (the timeZone of your business.json, UTC without it): the daily totals, the analytics ranges (from and to) and the analytics dashboard all use it, and GET /v1/analytics answers it as timeZone. Days already counted keep their day when the time zone changes. GET /v1/events/count and GET /v1/events/counts?by=type count the raw events with the list's own type filter.
events: Shop events are browser events on window. Ecommerce's shopper widgets send them; your own code may send them too. Growth records each one (Conversion funnel) and passes it to the pixels that are loaded: Meta (ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase), Google (view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase, and a purchase as your Google Ads conversion) and TikTok (ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, CompletePayment). Money is in minor units with its currency; pixels get major units.
page: Site searches are found on pages whose address has one of your search parameters (q, s, search, query by default); SSGrowth.search(term, { results }) records one from your code. A page that does not exist is recorded when it carries the not_found marker or calls SSGrowth.notFound(). Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB) are measured in the visitor's browser and sent when the page is left.
seo: robots.txt and the verification tags are served for your site to include: your server answers /robots.txt with what GET /v1/robots.txt gives (your rules plus a Sitemap line per sitemap) and adds the tags of GET /v1/verification to the page head. Search engines read them from your own domain.
indexnow: IndexNow tells Bing, Yandex and the other search engines that take it about new or changed pages at once. Set your key (8–128 letters, digits or dashes) in Settings and serve it as plain text at https://<your domain>/<key>.txt (GET /v1/indexnow/key.txt gives it). Submit addresses of your website with POST /v1/indexnow or the SEO checklist widget, when you ask; nothing is submitted by itself.
checklist: The SEO checklist reads your robots.txt, your sitemap and your pages when you ask (the widget's button or POST /v1/seo/checks) and checks each page: it opens, can be indexed, has a title, a meta description, one main heading, a canonical link, its language, the phone viewport, social sharing tags, image descriptions and structured data. Every check that does not pass comes with the steps to fix it (widget texts, editable in Settings → Texts).
notice: The notice bar shows your text and an optional link between the dates you set (checked on every page load). Place it with the notice_bar element, else it goes at the top of the page; visitors can close it for the rest of their visit if you allow it.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: the analytics dashboard (analytics.read) and the SEO checklist (seo.check; the IndexNow box with indexnow.submit). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain.
api: Every route answers JSON (robots.txt and the IndexNow key answer plain text); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
